summary: You sit bottom of the table on 79 points, so your GW4 claims process first if these players are still free when the window runs (waivers close 11 September). Same three claims as this morning, now re-sourced from permitted outlets after today's SOURCES-list purge stripped their citations: Igor Jesus for Marmoush (a value upgrade over a Marmoush who is himself trending toward more minutes, not a bench-risk drop), Le Fee for Barcola (Barcola still expected on the bench for tonight's Liverpool debut at Ipswich), and Rayan for Doku, now upgraded from a low-confidence hedge to medium - Doku's calf return points to around 13 September, after GW4's own deadline, so he would miss this entire window. The rest of the squad (Munoz, Milenkovic, Bijol, Gvardiol, Collins, Schade, Tavernier, Garner) are established starters this week and none clears the bar for a fourth or fifth swap.

claims.why: Igor Jesus is confirmed as Nottingham Forest's first-choice striker under new manager Oliver Glasner, ahead of Chris Wood, and Forest have started the season well. Marmoush's own case has actually improved since last night - Tottenham's Dominic Solanke has an ankle injury and hasn't played since early August, a major doubt this weekend, so the competition that clouded Marmoush's spot has eased and he is named in Tottenham's predicted XI at Forest on Friday. This is now a value upgrade (a confirmed #1 striker for free) rather than a bench-risk argument, so confidence is medium rather than high.
claims.model: Model has Igor Jesus at next5 14.3 (avail 0.95) versus Marmoush at 8.5 (avail 0.52) - a real gap, but Marmoush's own avail has already risen sharply since Solanke's injury became known, so the true gap is smaller than it looks; still worth the swap for Igor Jesus's superior nailed-on output.

claims.why: Barcola is still expected to start on the bench for his Liverpool debut against Ipswich tonight - manager Iraola has not ruled him in, and the latest predicted XI (published this morning) leaves him out of the starting eleven with Gakpo continuing on the left. Le Fee is a confirmed Sunderland starter in an attacking midfield role, so this is a straightforward swap of a bench-bound marquee name for a nailed starter while Barcola finds his feet.
claims.model: Model has Le Fee at next5 16.1 (avail 1.00) versus Barcola at 1.4 (avail 0.10) - the model has no career data on Barcola yet so it is essentially guessing zero, and tonight's team news supports that low number for now.

claims.why: Doku's calf return now points to around 13 September, per starters.json research this week - after GW4's own deadline (12 September), so he would miss this window entirely, not just be a doubt for it. Rayan is a proven attacking outlet who has produced directly against Newcastle before and gives a real floor while Doku's return drags past the deadline.
claims.model: Model has Rayan at next5 15.8 (avail 0.95) versus Doku at 3.5 (avail 0.00) - the model already has Doku's injury priced in, and the timeline now confirms he will not be back in time for GW4 either, which raises this from a pure hedge to a reasonably confident swap.

claims.why: Woltemade left Newcastle for Juventus on a season-long loan on deadline day, so he plays in Serie A, not the Premier League, until at least next summer - a mandatory drop, not a judgement call. Igor Jesus is confirmed as Forest's starting striker in their predicted XI for Friday's game against Tottenham.
claims.model: Model: Igor Jesus next5 14.5 vs Woltemade 0.3, +14.2. Fully agree - the loan has pushed Woltemade's number to essentially zero, the clearest drop in the squad.

claims.why: Eze is still stuck behind Arsenal's front line under Arteta with no sign of a minutes trend pointing up. Rayan is confirmed in Bournemouth's predicted attacking three alongside Kluivert and Tavernier for the Newcastle game, and is being talked up as a breakout name this season.
claims.model: Model: Rayan next5 16.2 vs Eze 8.0, +8.2. Agree with the model - Eze's bench role explains the gap and there is no sign of it closing.

sources.title: Could Bournemouth's Rayan become the Premier League's next Brazilian star?

claims.why: This is a hedge, not an urgent need. Garner's recovery from groin surgery is running ahead of schedule and he started for Everton in midweek against Preston, but Moyes still is not trusting him for a full 90 minutes. Gross is a fully fit, nailed-on Brighton starter with no fitness question at all. Only use this claim if you want the safer floor rather than Garner's upside.
claims.model: Model: Gross next5 16.0 vs Garner 10.1, +5.9. Partial overrule - the model cannot see Garner's accelerated recovery, so the real gap is probably smaller than 5.9, but Gross is nailed and Garner still is not.
